records.title: Each Way Nudge
records.history:
Loads going on with this one. Each Way Nudge has a stack of banknotes and coins in the middle of the top glass and a nudge ladder climbing each side of it, one pink and one green, both topping out at 10 nudges.

I snapped it at Retropolis Classic Amusements. It's 10p play, and the big disc at the top reads £5 with repeat chance. Down the right-hand side the features are named: Super Streak, Money Grabber, Note Shoot and Cash Belt, then Reel Money, 3 Reel Blasts, Coin Snake and Cash Dash on the lower glass.

The button row's a good one too: Hold, Hold Hi, Hold Lo, Swap Nudges and Death or Glory, plus Cancel/Collect and Start. There's a little Let's Play Barcrest badge in the bottom corner of the glass as well.

records.gameplay_guide: It's 10p a go on this one, for £5 with repeat chance. The reels have Hold, Hold Hi and Hold Lo buttons, and there's a Swap Nudges button to go with the two nudge ladders on the top glass. Barcrest's flyer says you nudge up and down for cash, with multiple repeats.

records.title: Each Way Nudge
records.history:
"Nudge up and down for great cash prizes." That's the first line on the flyer, and it's written next to a big pointing hand. The others go "Two trails to nudges – twice the chance", "Nudge your way to the jackpot" and "Multiple repeats!"

The name makes sense once you look at the glass. There's a nudge ladder either side of the cash artwork, both going up to 10 nudges. The cabinet pictured here is 10p play, playing for a fiver plus repeat chance.

It was Barcrest's game for the Genesis '98 cabinet, the one with the note acceptor, and the flyer says it ran on MPU5. Genesis options were £15 cash at 20p, 25p or 30p, £10 cash at the same three stakes, or £5 cash at anything from 5p to 30p.

Just don't get it mixed up with Each Way Nudger, which is a different machine with an annoyingly similar name.
